This document's whole value is that it can be trusted, and it is currently stale — critically, stale in the REASSURING direction in at least one place, which is the worst possible failure mode for an honesty inventory.

Your job is verification first, editing second. For EVERY entry in both tables ("Fixed since the last audit — verified, do not re-report these" and "Still not true — ranked by what it would cost a customer or admin"):
1. Open the file and line it cites. Confirm the claim is still true and the line number still points at the right code (this repo is edited constantly; line numbers drift).
2. Correct the line number, or move the entry between tables, or delete it, based on what you actually find. Never leave a citation you did not open.

Entries I have specific reason to believe are now WRONG — check these first, but do not trust my framing over what you find:

- **"Still not true" item 1: "There is no UI to save a card, so renewal auto-charge can never fire."** Card auto-charge was shipped since this was written. Check whether `lib/actions-payment-method.ts` (`startCardSetup`, `finalizeCardSetup`, `removeSavedCard`, `settleOutstanding`) now has real callers in `app/` or `components/`. If it does, this belongs in the Fixed table with the actual call sites cited.
- **"Still not true" item 2: "The hardened firewall is in the file, not in the kernel."** The hardened ruleset WAS applied. Verify against the LIVE ruleset with `nft list ruleset` (or `nft list chain inet nxeon input`) — do not infer from the script. Also note `scripts/firewall.nft` no longer reads `ADMIN_PORTS = { 22, 8006 }`; port 22 was deliberately moved into the public accept set after removing it from ADMIN_PORTS orphaned SSH entirely and tripped the auto-revert. Read the incident comment in that file and reflect what it actually says now. Confirm whether :8006 is in fact unreachable from the internet.
- **"Still not true" item 4: "Post-cutover TLS is never retried" (DEAD).** `sslSweep` is now registered in `worker/index.ts`. Check whether `runPostCutoverTls` (`worker/migrate.ts` around :260) is still reachable only from a commented-out enqueue, and whether the registered `sslSweep` now covers the case in practice. Report precisely which of the two is true — "the sweep covers it" and "the retry path is still dead" are different statements and the doc must not blur them.
- **The doc's claims about migration test coverage.** `test/migration-gate.test.ts` exists and currently passes 36/36. Anywhere the doc implies migration scoring is untested or untestable is wrong. Also `test/` now contains pricing-display-vs-charge, proration, wallet-split, migration-sizing, dunning-schedule, billing-terms, games, growth, rate-limit and totp test files, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now runs typecheck + tests on push and PR. If the doc says there is no CI or no test coverage, fix that.
- Every cited line number in the "Fixed" table. `worker/migrate-real.ts` in particular has been edited heavily today, so `judgeMigrationOutcome` is no longer at :2262.

Then ADD to the "Fixed" table the migration defects found by the first real end-to-end migration rehearsal (2026-07-26) and fixed today in `worker/migrate-real.ts`. Read the code and cite it accurately — do not copy my descriptions blind, verify each one:
- `clean()` stripped newlines and tabs, then six verification paths `.split("\n")` the result. `cleanLines()` now exists alongside `clean()` (read the incident comment on both). Fixed at `resolvesHere`, the `df` tail, and `unitState`'s `systemctl show` parse (which now anchors each KEY=value to its own line with `^…$`/`m`). The severe consequence: `resolvesHere` was always false, so a correctly-pointed domain was reported as not pointing at the new server and HTTP-01 certificate issuance was unreachable.
- The Docker inspect Go template aborted on `{{len .HostConfig.Devices}}`, which made docker emit nothing and the container vanish from the inventory. Now guarded, plus an authoritative `docker ps -aq | wc -l` count (`CCOUNT`) so a shortfall is detected rather than read as "no containers".
- `parseInventory` used to `.filter()` out containers whose name/image failed validation, which made `planContainer`'s own "not reproducible safely" blockers unreachable.
- The nginx/apache `server_name` harvest scanned commented-out lines and un-symlinked `sites-available/`, injecting phantom domains into the score's denominator and making a `COMPLETED` outcome unreachable.
- `/home` was in `DEFAULT_PATHS` (`lib/actions-migrate.ts:110`) AND in `UNSAFE_EXACT` (`worker/migrate-real.ts`), so the default selection shown to every customer was silently discarded. It is now expanded per-user with collisions named, and any refused path is reported instead of dropped.
- `preflightUnitExecs` symlinked a missing interpreter to whatever the target had and called it "the same program" without comparing versions (Node 20 → Node 12). Now compares major versions via the new `majorVersion()` and `UnitExecHost.versionOf`/`versionOnSource`, and a mismatch blocks with the right install command.
- `judgeMigrationOutcome` ignored steps with `status: "failed"` entirely — a failed database restore could score COMPLETED. It now takes `failedSteps` and `unreadContainers`.
- The report gave contradictory DNS instructions ("point the DNS, then run certbot" vs "do not move DNS for these names yet") with no way to tell which applied to which name. There is now one explicit ordered cutover block, and certificate issuance is stated as automatic.

Style rules: match the existing document's voice exactly — specific, plain, no marketing tone, every claim carrying a `file:line` citation. Keep the classification vocabulary (WORKS / SIMULATED / UNVERIFIED SUCCESS / SAVED-BUT-UNREAD / DEAD / PARTIAL). Keep the "Still not true" list ranked by customer/admin cost. Preserve the warning that concurrent agents edit the tree.

Also check the two "user action still outstanding" items are recorded somewhere in the doc, because they are the only unrecovered risks: (a) `dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` must be published with Mailcow's key and `nxeon._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` deleted — platform transactional email is currently UNSIGNED because a cleanup instruction deleted the real record; (b) `OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` or `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` is unset, so backups are single-site. If they are not in the doc, add them where an operator will see them.

Do NOT edit any file other than `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`. Do not build, deploy, restart services, or commit — I am doing that. Other agents are editing `lib/resize.ts`, `lib/wallet-split.ts`, `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx`, `tsconfig.json` and files under `test/` concurrently, so read those but expect churn and cite what you see.

Report: a table of every entry you checked and its verdict (confirmed / line corrected / moved tables / deleted), what you added, and anything you could not verify and therefore left flagged.

name: CI

# Typecheck + unit tests on every push and every pull request. Nothing here
# touches Proxmox, Stripe, Mailcow, a database or the network beyond the npm
# registry: the whole suite is pure functions (test/*.test.ts).
on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
  pull_request:
    branches: ["**"]

# A newer push to the same ref cancels the older run.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    name: typecheck + tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      # `prisma generate` and `import "@prisma/client"` want the variable to
      # exist; nothing in CI ever connects. This is not a real host.
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://ci:ci@127.0.0.1:5432/ci?schema=public
      # Keep the suite honest about being offline/deterministic.
      CI: "true"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # The Prisma client is generated, not committed. Type-checking `lib/**`
      # (and importing lib/mailer.ts from the dunning test) needs the generated
      # model types, so this must run before tsc and before the tests. Generation
      # reads prisma/schema.prisma only — it never contacts a database.
      - name: Generate Prisma client
        run: npx prisma generate

      - name: Typecheck (tsc --noEmit)
        run: |
          # tsc currently reports TS5097 for every `import … from "../lib/x.ts"`
          # in test/*.test.ts: the tests import with an explicit .ts extension
          # (which the `tsx --test` runner requires) while the tsconfig does not
          # set `allowImportingTsExtensions`. Those lines are the established,
          # pre-existing exception in this repo — everything else must be clean.
          #
          # The filter is deliberately narrower than the `grep -v "test/.*test.ts"`
          # convention used by hand: it drops ONLY TS5097 lines from test files, so
          # a genuine type error in a test still fails this job.
          npx tsc --noEmit > tsc.log 2>&1 || true
          grep -vE '^test/[^ ]+\.test\.ts\([0-9]+,[0-9]+\): error TS5097:' tsc.log > tsc-unexpected.log || true
          if [ -s tsc-unexpected.log ]; then
            echo "::error::tsc reported errors outside the known TS5097 test-import exception"
            cat tsc-unexpected.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Typecheck clean ($(grep -c 'TS5097' tsc.log || true) known TS5097 test-import lines suppressed)."

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Upload typecheck log on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tsc-log
          path: tsc.log
          if-no-files-found: ignore
